description: Save a fact, preference or decision so a later conversation can recall it. Use it when the user asks you to remember something, and whenever the user states a fact, preference or decision worth keeping. Required: `text`. Optional: `tags`, `speaker`, `object_type`, `partition`, `supersedes`, `relations`, `inferred`, `similar_min_relevance`. Returns `key`. Separate from Claude's built-in memory. `partition_use` sets the session's default partition. Set `speaker: "user"` when the text is the user's own words. Correct an earlier memory with `supersedes: <key>`; `forget` on the new key reverts. `similar` lists up to 3 close existing memories; `suggested_forget` names a near-exact duplicate you may forget. `inferred: true` saves your own inference, hidden from default results until reviewed. `object_type` is a free-text label. Long text is split into pieces; `key` still works for `expand`/`forget`. Never store secrets.

inferred.description: True for your own inference rather than something the user stated; hidden until reviewed.

object_type.description: Optional free-text label for what kind of memory.

relations.description: Optional edges from this new memory to existing ones.

speaker.description: `user` for the user's own words, `assistant` for yours.

supersedes.description: Optional: the key of an existing memory this one corrects or replaces.

tags.description: Optional tags to attach to this memory.

name: remember
title: Save a memory
